editorialInterpretation: B2 is independent reading of contemporary prose and reports with viewpoints, following extended argument on familiar domains. Length alone does not make a text B2.
Each story should develop two or more competing priorities and a causally specific outcome, with meaningful dialogue and concrete narrative events rather than a padded essay.

Use varied conjunctions and coherent reference, concessive and conditional reasoning, relative clauses, passive constructions and reported viewpoints naturally; no per-story grammar checklist imposed as certification.
Keep rare idioms and jargon limited, inferable or glossed. Standard German narration can vary pace for speakers but should not claim pronunciation assessment.
Translate the entire German story faithfully into English and sentence translations. Current earlier story english fields sometimes began as summaries; do not reproduce this shortcut for B2.
Comprehension should test causal links, competing viewpoints, implication and specific decisions, alongside factual detail. Keep every answer supported by text with plausible unambiguous distractors.
Choose approximately 940–960 words initially to allow edits; count final displayed German story with app readingWordCount; title/questions/glosses do not count.
These 200 unique title and conflict/resolution designs are proposals, not a guarantee of semantic non-overlap. Some adjacent themes intentionally recur; story causality must not.

overlapRisks.risk: Lost keys, hats, cards, parcels or wrong dates becoming long stories
Basic repair complaint, estimates, photo/report, or corrected review
Changing a family feast to reduce mothers work; bilingual celebration; failed surprise
Simple shared balcony, cleaning rota, or new roommate negotiation
Group assignment labor imbalance, phone use, wrong quote, overly full study plan
Travel brochures misleading, slower group pace, network-free ticket, changed weather
Choosing cheaper products, inspecting used bike, unnecessary discount, sharing a budget
Photo privacy, phishing, backups, excessive app permissions, notification boundaries
Recipe adaptations, needs-specific menus, leftovers and simplifying a cooking evening

deduplicationRecommendations: Validate exact title/body identity and normalized paragraph/sentence hashes against all 454 existing stories and within B2.
Compute token/character n-gram similarity to surface copied prose; flag long shared spans beyond routine German formulas.
Compare plot summaries as tuples of trigger, stakeholders, information gap, competing priorities, decision, cost and outcome across all levels; renamed people or objects do not make a new plot.
Use semantic similarity only as a review queue; universal rejection thresholds can wrongly reject a shared domain while missing paraphrased plots.
Review nearest existing stories for every B2 draft before audio. Reject reused narrative structures, especially universal ending of discuss, create plan, reflect.
Editorial review should compare each ten-story category internally and rotate voice, viewpoint, chronology, number of speakers, outcome and emotional tone.
Record audio input text hash and sentence translation source hash; finalize text first and regenerate dependent outputs if edits change spoken words.
No automated metric can prove every plot across 654 stories semantically unique or certify CEFR B2. Report measured exact and near-duplicate checks plus the actual scope of human/editorial review.

plotBeats: A bicycle wheel catches on the old courtyard step during an ordinary arrival; the resident laughs until a neighbor explains why she avoids that entrance entirely.
At a sample paving demonstration, cycle users see the chance for covered storage while another resident imagines independently entering her own home.

A forgotten strip behind a former parking bay offers a second storage location, but converting it removes two desirable parking spaces.
The organizer presents the real trade-off openly; one car owner objects, and the agreement remains partial rather than magically unanimous.
Work finishes with a continuous corridor and relocated racks; a resident enters carrying ordinary shopping without asking someone to lift it, while the bicycle advocate walks a little farther.

plotBeats: Two partners stand in a kitchen showroom, delighted by a design that will make their small flat look unusually spacious.
An evening at home shows one partner editing paid work on the dining table while the other quietly clears away materials to serve dinner.
When the designer removes the old small room from the plan, the working partner falls silent instead of risking the shared excitement.

In the altered flat, one partner closes a door for a call while the other starts dinner, and the smaller visible room finally serves both lives.
